thread_analysis.thread_summary: This thread is the fuller, later-stage continuation of the same GO Corporation (contact Satoshi Yonezawa) Bluetooth certification engagement already documented in thread_0242 — same Silicon Labs BLE module, same module/stack Component QDID Consistency Check issue and resolution. Thread_0238 carries that history forward to completion: order placement (April 2025), USD wire transfer proxy, Compliance Folder document preparation (operation manual format questions), Review Page confirmation, Submission, and final Compliance Folder (CD-R plus electronic Index.pdf version) delivery completing the engagement (May 27, 2025).
all_questions_found: (Duplicate of thread_0242_case_01) Does the module's 'Component (Tested)' status require additional software-layer testing?
(Duplicate of thread_0242_case_02) Are detailed module-engineering documents required, or only whole-product documents?
(Duplicate of thread_0242_case_03) How to resolve the LL/RFPHY Consistency Check inconsistency from combining the module and stack QDIDs?
How long does registration take from order to completion, including wire transfer proxy? (see thread_0238_case_01)
Should Compliance Folder documents be in English, what format should the operation manual follow, and is datasheet transcription sufficient for antenna documentation? (see thread_0238_case_02)
thread_analysis.key_technical_discussion: The early technical content in this thread (module test exemption logic, document scope, Consistency Check resolution via vendor Subset DN) duplicates thread_0242 and is not re-extracted as new cases here to avoid duplication. This thread's new content covers the practical post-order execution: a staged timeline (wire transfer transit, registration processing, Compliance Folder preparation) and Compliance Folder document format guidance, most concretely resolved via a reference example (an existing Bluetooth TAG product's user manual) for the operation manual's expected pairing-procedure-focused format.
thread_analysis.key_decision_logic: See thread_0238_case_01 and thread_0238_case_02 for the new decision logic in this thread; the duplicated technical content's decision logic is documented in thread_0242's case files.
thread_analysis.consulting_mistake: Two of the customer's three document-preparation questions (document language requirement, antenna datasheet transcription sufficiency) do not appear to have received an explicit written confirmation in this thread — only the operation manual format question was clearly answered via a concrete reference example. While the customer's assumptions on the other two points went unchallenged through to project completion, this is a weaker form of confirmation than an explicit written answer, and represents a minor gap worth flagging for future similar inquiries.
thread_analysis.consulting_takeaway: This thread reinforces thread_0242's takeaway about verifying vendor-originated Consistency Check fixes, and adds a new lesson: when a customer raises several document-preparation sub-questions together, ensure each one receives an explicit written answer rather than letting some be implicitly confirmed only by the absence of later correction.
